name: Icy Veins
author: Icy Veins guide writers
methodology: Broad-meta tier lists per role and bracket, aimed at the general player population.
summary: A guide site's own letter grades for the live patch, written by its spec authors. Editorial judgement, not measured play.

name: Method
author: Tactyks (M+); Method raiders (raid)
methodology: Top-end lens: M+ list by Tactyks, raid list written with Method raiders from a race-to-world-first output perspective.
notes: Raid list omits Vengeance DH (not ranked on the page). Method's list content is unchanged since its 2026-03-31 revision; re-verified live and era-confirmed (Devourer present) 2026-07-09.
summary: Letter grades from a world-first raiding guild's guide team. Its M+ list currently publishes no S tier at all, so its ceiling is a grade lower than everyone else's.

name: Wowhead
author: Wowhead class writers
methodology: Rankings for all classes based on Raid and Mythic+ performance; also the primary PTR datamining source for 12.1 class tuning and tier-set changes.
summary: Letter grades from a large guide site, written per role and bracket by its guide authors.

name: Archon
author: Archon.gg (statistical)
methodology: Statistical tier lists computed from Warcraft Logs parses and Blizzard leaderboards — 14-day rolling window, refreshed daily. Raid tiers read from the throughput metric tier list (NOT the default popularity grouping); M+ tiers from the M+ score tier list. EARLY-S2 BASIS (owner decision 2026-08-25): the raid letters come from the HEROIC throughput list while Mythic is sparse — Heroic carries ~170x the parses and covers all 27 DPS specs where Mythic held 6 specs under 10 parses and no Fire Mage at all. Switch back to the Mythic list (a reviewed registry edit + CONSENSUS_VERSION bump) once Mythic reaches 27/27 DPS with healthy samples. The Mythic rankings pages stay registered as ancillary metric feeds. Mirrored at u.gg/wow.
notes: Fetch recipe: parse the __NEXT_DATA__ JSON script tag from raw HTML (WebFetch markdown drops it). Raid pages carry three tierLists (popularity/throughput/survivability) — use metric "throughput"; M+ pages use metric "score". The Heroic raid pages (the letter basis since 2026-08-25) parse with the IDENTICAL recipe — only the /heroic/ path segment differs; the ancillary Mythic rankings pages feed the "(Mythic)" numeric families and survivability. Mirrored at u.gg/wow.
summary: Letter grades computed from logged play. Raid tiers come from its THROUGHPUT list and M+ tiers from its SCORE list — never the default popularity grouping, which ranks how often a spec is played rather than how it performs.

name: WoWMeta
author: Hypermeta Network (algorithmic)
methodology: Population-wide Mythic+ statistics from the official Blizzard M+ API. The tracker ingests lowerBound (the lower bound of the 95% CI of a spec's MEAN Blizzard M+ rating across all logged players) as a number — deliberately NOT as letter tiers. Retyped from tier-list to metrics on 2026-07-31: the site's published letters are Ckmeans clusters of an undocumented "Popular Choice" / "Optimized Potential" toggle that defaults to PLAYER COUNT, so its letters ranked representation rather than performance (Augmentation had the highest lb_ci of all 27 M+ DPS specs while sitting in B; Retribution was 15th and sat in S). Distinct from Murlok's top-50 ceiling and Archon's Warcraft Logs top-end: this is a sample-size-penalised population MEAN, not a ceiling.

pages.label: Raid · DPS (live upstream, but lowerBound is DPS throughput — not ingested)
Raid · Healer (live upstream, but lowerBound is DPS throughput — not ingested)
Raid · Tank (live upstream, but lowerBound is DPS throughput — not ingested)

notes: Fetch the JSON API directly, NOT the web page: https://data.wowmeta.com/rankings/midnight/mplus/all/0.json (one file backs all three M+ pages) plus https://data.wowmeta.com/manifest.json for snapshotDate (= the page's "Last updated", and the honest asOf). Plain curl, no headers, no proxy. Select blocks by categoryType in {dps,hps,tank} + sortField "lowerBound" + keyRange undefined — WHITELIST those three, since "melee"/"ranged" are subsets of dps and would double-count. The wowmeta.com HTML is a STALE S3 prerender (dateModified 2026-03-23) and r.jina.ai is non-deterministic about executing the page JS — neither is a trustworthy transport. The raid endpoint (/rankings/midnight/raid/all-bosses/5.json) is live but its lowerBound is DPS THROUGHPUT (~180k), a different quantity on a different scale — do not merge it under the M+ rating name.
summary: The lower bound of a 95% confidence interval on a spec's MEAN Blizzard M+ rating across every logged player. A sample-size-penalised population average — not a ceiling, and not what the top of the ladder is doing.

name: Warcraft Logs
author: Warcraft Logs aggregate statistics
methodology: Per-spec aggregate combat-log statistics: median (50th percentile) rDPS/HPS and parse counts. LIVE Season 2 raid = zone 53 "The Venomous Abyss" (partition 1 = 12.1, Mythic difficulty 5, size 20, 9 encounters); live S2 M+ = zone 55 (partition 1 = Season 2, difficulty 10, size 5) — both enumerated 2026-08-14, frozen until content opens. Retired-cycle zones, kept as history: S1 raid = zone 46 (Mythic difficulty 5, size 20, partition 3 = 12.0.7 — the zone's DEFAULT partition has since moved to 4 = 12.1, so recipes must pin 3); S1 M+ = zone 47 (difficulty 10, size 5, partition 1); zone 54 was the 12.1 PTR raid and zone 56 the 12.1 PTR M+ — PTR-quality, era-tagged "ptr", kept out of live baselines. Sanctioned long-term access is the v2 GraphQL API (free OAuth client), which DOES serve the PTR zones — the nightly reads zones 52/54/56 through it every run, so an earlier note here claiming "PTR zones are HTML-only" was wrong and is corrected (2026-08-08); it would have misdirected the Season-2 zone-discovery run into a transport we do not need. What the API does not currently serve is the rDPS metric family, which has returned a bare "Internal server error" since 2026-07-12 while metric dps on the same encounter returns normally. HTML statistics tables are the fallback for exactly that gap, fetched fresh every run (policy 2026-07-08: no at-most-daily cap) — but datacenter IPs are Cloudflare-blocked on the HTML endpoint, and as of 2026-08-08 the residential path is challenged too, so the rDPS series are currently unreachable by either transport.

12.1 PTR raid testing (zone 54, The Venomous Abyss)
12.1 PTR Dummy Dome (zone 52, fixed target counts)

summary: Median damage or healing across every logged pull, by role and bracket. rDPS strips out damage credited to external buffs, so it measures a player's own contribution rather than what their raid lent them.

name: Murlok.io
author: Murlok.io (Blizzard API leaderboard data)
methodology: Average M+ rating of each spec's own top-50 rated players (US/EU/KR/TW, refreshed ~8h). This is a top-end ceiling measure — NOT representation share and NOT a strength tier; every spec always samples exactly 50 players. Never convert to letter grades.
summary: The average rating of each spec's best FIFTY players — a ceiling, showing what the spec achieves in expert hands. It says nothing about how popular a spec is or how it plays for everyone else.

name: Bloodmallet (SimC)
author: Bloodmallet / SimulationCraft (tier MID2)
methodology: SimulationCraft per-spec simulations, refreshed ~daily. Target-count scaling (talent_target_scaling chart: DPS at 1/2/3/…/15 targets, best build per count) powers the fight-type profiles for DPS specs. Sim DPS is point-in-time and build-dependent — display as numbers, never letters. JSON API: bloodmallet.com/chart/get/{chart}/{fight_style}/{snake_case_class}/{spec}.
summary: SimulationCraft damage against a fixed target dummy at several target counts. Theoretical output under perfect play with pre-set gear — a shape, not a prediction of your parse.

name: Mythicstats
author: raptoranka
methodology: Weekly per-spec M+ meta statistics from the top 2000 keys of each reset period: representation % per spec (the meta-share axis Murlok cannot provide), spec diversity by key level, top comps. JS-heavy — fetch via r.jina.ai proxy.
summary: How often each spec appears among the highest Mythic+ keys of the week. A presence measure at the very top end, so it reflects what the best groups choose as much as what performs.

name: Blizzard 12.1 PTR notes
author: Blizzard (Linxy) — official PTR development notes
methodology: Canonical source for 12.1 tuning: the 'Midnight: Curse of Ula'tek PTR Development Notes' forum thread. Each PTR build's changes arrive as a new reply post (~weekly). Machine-readable via Discourse JSON (append .json). New waves are discovered via the Wowhead news RSS (exact pubDates), filtered for '12.1 PTR' + Development Notes/Class Tuning/Datamined. A new patch cycle means a NEW thread — re-discover per patch.
summary: Blizzard's own PTR build notes and patch notes — the primary record of what changed. Where the shipping notes disagree with an earlier PTR build, the notes win.

name: Community
author: Class Discords + verified creators (data/community.json)
methodology: Qualitative layer: 13 class Discords (links only — content not fetchable, auth + TOS) and 1-2 verified creators per class whose video transcripts feed cited creator takes (data/creator-takes.json). Opinion, never tier data.

pages.label: Verified creators → takes in spec drawers

summary: Class Discords, community sites and creators, verified by hand. Opinion and analysis, kept firmly out of the tier consensus.

name: SimulationCraft
author: SimC project nightly (engine-official)
methodology: Official nightly MID2_Raid Patchwerk report (the report name follows the sim tier: MID1_Raid through Season 1, MID2_Raid since the 2026-09-03 wholesale adoption): one fixed high-ilvl profile per spec/hero-variant, iterations=7500 — we ingest the best variant per DPS spec as 'SimC nightly Patchwerk DPS'. Pure single-target, fixed gear: a sim baseline, not a rankings verdict (the project itself disclaims class comparisons — keep it a number, never a tier).
notes: Parse the .txt variant (plain text ranking of ~43 MID2_{Class}_{Spec}_{HeroVariant} profiles). Filter to DPS-role roster specs (tanks appear at low DPS; healers absent; Augmentation has no profile — unsimmable support spec).
summary: The SimulationCraft project's own nightly raid report. Theoretical damage under a standard profile — the same caveat as any sim: perfect play, fixed gear.

name: Raidbots
methodology: User-run cloud SimC (Top Gear, Droptimizer, Quick Sim) — the canonical place to sim YOUR character. No public per-spec aggregates (re-verified 2026-07-01), so reference only.
summary: A tool for simulating YOUR character rather than an average one. Linked as a next step; nothing here is ingested from it.

name: QE Live
methodology: Voulk's healer gearing/trinket evaluation tool (all healer specs). Client-side SPA — no fetchable data, but actively maintained for Midnight (verified via its GitHub repo, 12.0.7 branches). Reference for the healer audience; the blog publishes dated Midnight healer articles (e.g. S1 embellishment tier list).
summary: A healer-focused gear and stat tool. Linked as a next step; nothing here is ingested from it.

name: Liquid Armory
methodology: SimulationCraft-driven guild-simmed trinket and best-in-slot data. A gearing axis, not a spec-strength axis — linked as an external reference, never rendered as a tier column.
summary: A raiding guild's armory and guide hub. Linked as a next step; nothing here is ingested from it.

name: Robydoby
author: Robydoby (Arctic Avengers, EU-Kazzak) — community theorycrafter; the sheet asks for a visible link wherever it is used
methodology: Curated per-encounter aggregation of Warcraft Logs 12.1 PTR raid-testing (zone 54) parses: per-spec 90th/95th/99th percentile raw DPS/HPS (separate DPS and Healer sheets) with quality filters (min fight length, optional kills-only). A top-end percentile view that complements the tracker's own pooled per-player medians — numbers only, never a tier.
